questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Iron-rich dust gives Mars its reddish appearance.

questions.question: What is 12 × 8?
Which part of a plant absorbs water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil.

questions.question: Which word is a noun?
questions.explanation: A noun names a person, place, thing or idea. Mountain names a thing.

questions.question: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.explanation: The prefix hexa- means six.

questions.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

questions.question: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight to make sugars.

questions.question: What is three quarters written as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 3 divided by 4 is 0.75.

questions.question: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
questions.explanation: William Shakespeare wrote this play in the 1590s.

questions.question: What force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity attracts objects with mass toward each other.

questions.question: How many degrees are in a right angle?
questions.explanation: A right angle is one quarter of a full 360-degree turn.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
questions.explanation: The heart contracts to pump blood through blood vessels.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris is the capital of France.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is prime?
questions.explanation: 23 has exactly two positive factors: 1 and 23.

questions.question: What do we call water changing from liquid to gas?
questions.explanation: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapor.

questions.question: Which punctuation mark ends a question?
questions.explanation: A direct question ends with a question mark (?).

questions.question: What is 144 divided by 12?
On which continent is Egypt?
questions.explanation: Egypt is primarily in northeast Africa; its Sinai Peninsula is in Asia.

questions.question: Which is the smallest unit of life?
questions.explanation: Cells are the basic structural and functional units of living things.

questions.question: What is the past tense of go?
questions.explanation: Go is an irregular verb. Its simple past tense is went.

questions.question: How many centimeters make one meter?
questions.explanation: Centi- means one hundredth, so 100 centimeters = 1 meter.

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is our closest star.

questions.question: Which fraction is equivalent to one half?
questions.explanation: Divide both 4 and 8 by 4 to get 1/2.

questions.question: What is the process by which a caterpillar becomes a butterfly?
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis changes an animal’s body as it develops.

questions.question: What is the main job of the lungs?
questions.explanation: Lungs take oxygen into the blood and remove carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is replenished naturally, unlike fossil fuels.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a square with 5 cm sides?
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides. 4 × 5 = 20 cm.

questions.question: Which word means the opposite of ancient?
questions.explanation: Modern means relating to the present or recent times.

questions.question: What instrument measures temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.question: Which layer of Earth do we live on?
questions.explanation: The crust is Earth’s thin outermost solid layer.
